clue.text: Bend on road to Lancaster, for example

parts.note: to bend out of shape is to warp
a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: Directions about a bend on the road to the city of Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster looks like the English city, but here it is the Avro Lancaster, the famous British Second World War bomber. In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avro Lancaster was a heavy bomber, an example of a military aircraft.

clue.text: See 18
Bit of a gut for Goon (pronounced)

indicators.note: pronounced signals that the word is to be said aloud, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: Harry Secombe was one of the Goons, the comedy team of the BBC radio Goon Show

explanation.surface: A request for a word describing a gut, said in the style of a Goon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a 1950s British radio comedy starring Spike Milligan, Peter Sellers and Harry Secombe; the surname Secombe is said the same way as the gut part.
explanation.definitionFit: The caecum is a pouch at the start of the large intestine, so a section of the bowel.

clue.text: Balfour's first novel abused by smears

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the name Balfour
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of the next word are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: A novel by Balfour gets savaged and smeared by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book Balfour wrote, but it is the anagram signal. Arthur Balfour was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To daub is to smear paint or dirt, so the verb with a prefix is a synonym of smears.

clue.text: Number after kinky fun, as free

indicators.note: after places the number at the end, following the rearranged letters
kinky means twisted, so the letters of fun are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Some numbers follow kinky fun, as people break free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' gives UNF from FUN; 'after' says the number comes behind the rest. 'Free' here is a verb, to release.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten something is to undo it, setting it loose or free.

clue.text: Non-U commendation about pain given to study of antiquities

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the commendation goes round the pain and the link
Non-U says the letter U is to be removed from the word that follows

parts.note: a eulogy is a speech of praise or commendation
gyp is informal British for pain, as in 'my back is giving me gyp'
given to supplies the short word to

explanation.surface: An upper-class snob refuses to praise someone who devotes painful effort to old relics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' is a British term for not upper-class, but here it says drop a U, leaving ELOGY; 'about' wraps that round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptology is the study of ancient Egypt, its antiquities and monuments.

clue.text: Run to show all right when beset by cut

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the right sits inside the cut

parts.note: a steak is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: A runner is shown to be all right when attacked by a slashing blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all right' suggests OK, but only 'right' is needed (R); 'all' belongs to the definition, since a streaker runs naked showing everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to run naked in public, showing all one has.

clue.text: Wreck shoe, turn grey

parts.note: a sabot is a wooden clog or shoe
to age is to grow old, turning grey

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a shoe and goes grey with worry.
explanation.walkthrough: Sabotage is said to come from the French sabot, the clog workers threw into machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: To sabotage something is to deliberately wreck or damage it.

clue.text: Day nothing changed?

parts.note: take the day and change everything about it, and you arrive at its opposite, the dark hours

explanation.surface: A question whether this day passed with nothing changing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question invites the solver to change a day completely, turning it into its opposite; the letters of 'nothing' without the O (nothing) can also be rearranged to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours are the opposite of day, what day becomes when wholly altered.

clue.text: Slip without leader into recess

indicators.note: without leader means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or small mistake

explanation.surface: Someone slips headlong into a recess.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess, typically at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Fruit and bread wrapped in parcels, distributed

indicators.note: wrapped in places the bread inside the rearranged parcels
distributed means spread around, so the letters of parcels are scattered into a new order

parts.note: a bap is a soft British bread roll

explanation.surface: Fruit and bread rolls are wrapped up in parcels and handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' scrambles the parcels to CRAPLES, and 'wrapped in' sets the bread roll after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Crab apples are small sour fruits of the wild apple tree.

clue.text: Ally during controversial US conflict briefly seeing what was used in it

indicators.note: during places the ally inside the shortened war's name

parts.note: Nam is the short name for Vietnam, the controversial US war
a pal is a friend or ally

explanation.surface: A friend serving in the Vietnam War witnesses the weapons deployed there.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers back to the clue's own war: the incendiary jelly dropped in Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm, a jellied incendiary, was used notoriously by US forces in Vietnam.

clue.text: Strong desire to make dark hairdo more light-headed, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is to be said aloud for a sound-alike

parts.note: an Afro is a hairstyle common among people with dark hair, and dizzier means more light-headed

explanation.surface: Advice on making a dark hairstyle even more giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Afro dizzier' said aloud sounds like the word for sexual desire, named after Aphrodite.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodisia is intense sexual desire, a strong longing.

clue.text: Bottom (not ticks …)

parts.note: the phrase 'not X but Y' gives but as the word set against not
a clock goes tick then tock, so in place of ticks come their partners

explanation.surface: A coy note insisting the bottom has nothing to do with insects.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'not ticks but tocks': the clue's ellipsis invites completing it with the partner of 'tick' in a clock's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttocks are the two rounded parts of the body forming the bottom.

clue.text: Piano with E# (accidental), possibly

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

indicators.note: accidental suggests something happening by chance, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the symbol # is read as sharp, giving E sharp

explanation.surface: A piano piece with an E sharp, an accidental in music, might be played.
explanation.walkthrough: In music an accidental is a sharp or flat outside the key, but here 'accidental' is the anagram signal: E SHARP becomes ERHAPS after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps is an adverb meaning maybe, a synonym for possibly.

clue.text: Wee weeing

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is trifling or small; the other is the informal verb for passing water.
explanation.definitionFit: Piddling means trivial and tiny, and also urinating, in British slang.

clue.text: Embrace popular Swedish product curtailed, back to massage

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, losing the last letter

parts.note: Volvo cars are made in Sweden

indicators.note: back to means the rear or last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A trendy Swedish gadget, cut short, is used for a back massage.
explanation.definitionFit: To involve is to include or take in, a sense of embrace.

clue.text: Alfred the Great's exceptional home economics report?

parts.note: very can mean extreme or exceptional, as in 'the very best'
a teacher's report on cookery might read 'well done'

explanation.surface: Praise for King Alfred's outstanding cookery class.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says King Alfred, sheltering in a peasant's hut, let the cakes burn: they were overcooked, so his were well past done.
explanation.definitionFit: The cakes Alfred the Great famously burnt were cooked far too long.

clue.text: Order in force demonstrating commitment

indicators.note: in places the order inside the word for force

parts.note: to prise something is to force it open
OM stands for the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An order in force shows a firm commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order in force' reads as a legal order being in effect, but Order is OM and force is PRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A promise is a commitment to do something.

clue.text: Instrument, one with register

definitions.meaning: a woodwind instrument played with the fingers over holes
someone who keeps a register or official record, also a type of judge

explanation.walkthrough: A register is also a musical range, which makes the second sense seem to belong with the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A recorder is a wind instrument and also someone who records events in a register.

clue.text: Brussels fanatic almost given the chop: operation cancelled, though his wasn't

definitions.text: Brussels fanatic almost given the chop: operation cancelled, though his wasn't

parts.note: Brussels is home to the EU's headquarters, so the city stands for the European Union

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic

indicators.note: cancelled means removed, so the operation is taken out of chop

parts.note: chop is used as written

explanation.surface: A Eurofanatic nearly gets the sack when an operation is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims NUT to NU, and 'cancelled' takes OP from CHOP to leave CH. Read whole, the clue describes a castrated man: his operation was not cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A eunuch is a man who has been castrated, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Rock once found beside quite a few strata

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, quite a few
Ayers Rock is the former name of Uluru in Australia

explanation.surface: Geologists find old rock beside many strata.
explanation.walkthrough: Uluru in central Australia was formerly called Ayers Rock; 'beside' sets L first.
explanation.definitionFit: Layers are strata, bands of rock laid one on another.

clue.text: Change to be topless: twelve topless shows extravagance

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: flux is constant change

indicators.note: topless again cuts off the first letter

parts.note: a jury is made up of twelve people

explanation.surface: Wanting to go topless, twelve topless dancers put on a lavish show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes F from FLUX and J from JURY: LUX + URY.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxury is lavish, extravagant living or an indulgence.

clue.text: Diversion to the left, I'm across, nearly up, then …

parts.note: an antic is a playful caper or amusing diversion
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
read as 'a cross', which is an X

explanation.surface: A traffic diversion to the left: the speaker crosses almost to the top, then...
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs into the next clue: getting nearly up and then going down is a letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: An anticlimax is a disappointing let-down after building up to something.

clue.text: … blue sort of clue

definitions.meaning: blue means sad or low in spirits
crossword clues come as across and the other direction

explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from 23 across, completing its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Down means depressed or blue, and it is also one of two kinds of crossword clue.

clue.text: Part of pound — I mean part of dollar

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone explains currency: a bit of a pound, sorry, a bit of a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'pounD I MEan'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is a ten-cent coin, a tenth of a US dollar.

clue.text: Dog killer captures Rex

indicators.note: captures means holds inside, so the king goes into the killer

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in the Bible
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A dog's killer catches a pet named Rex.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex looks like a dog's name, but it is R, from Latin for king.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a small Scottish terrier, a breed of dog.

clue.text: Gas about, talk incoherently and make message unintelligible

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the gas's letters are read backwards

parts.note: CS gas is a tear gas used in riot control
to ramble is to talk at length without coherence

explanation.surface: Someone gassing on, talking nonsense, garbles the message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' suggests chatter, but it is CS gas, a tear gas.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble a signal is to encode it so it cannot be understood.
